chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from al-Nawfali, from al-Sakuni, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) that

the Prophet (may Allah's blessings be upon him and his family) sent a brigade. So when they returned, he said: 'Welcome to the people who have accomplished the smaller jihad, and there remains the greater jihad.' It was said: 'O Messenger of Allah (may Allah's blessings be upon him and his family), what is the greater jihad?' He said: 'The jihad of the self.'

key_terms.النَّفْس: The self, soul, or ego — the inner dimension of the human being that must be disciplined
key_terms.جِهَادُ الْأَصْغَر: The lesser/smaller jihad — armed struggle in defense of the faith
key_terms.جِهَادُ الْأَكْبَر: The greater jihad — the internal struggle against the ego and base desires (jihad al-nafs)
key_terms.سَرِيَّة: A military expedition or detachment sent out by the Prophet without him personally leading it

ai.seo_question: What did the Prophet Muhammad say is the greater jihad after returning from battle?
ai.summary: This hadith records a famous prophetic saying distinguishing between two types of jihad. When warriors returned from battle, the Prophet (saww) welcomed them but noted that a greater struggle remained — the jihad al-nafs, the internal striving against one's own ego, desires, and moral failings. This teaching reflects the Shia ethical tradition's emphasis on inner purification as the highest form of spiritual effort, surpassing even armed conflict.
